prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Mathematical Notation Reference (language en).
Grid: 4 columns × 6 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 17px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Symbol" · longest unbreakable word 61px · one-line width 61px
  col 2: header "Name" · longest unbreakable word 87px · one-line width 116px
  col 3: header "LaTeX" · longest unbreakable word 66px · one-line width 66px
  col 4: header "Meaning" · longest unbreakable word 111px · one-line width 1320px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 584px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 583px.
Fixed: content, font, 17px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"Provide a reference linking mathematical symbols to their names, LaTeX commands, and meanings.","reading":"Readers can scan the symbol column to locate an entry, then read across for its name, command, and explanation; they may also compare names or commands down their columns.","groups":["Symbol, Name, and LaTeX identify the same notation in three forms.","Meaning explains each notation and contains the longest prose."],"keep_intact":["Symbols and LaTeX commands","Individual words in names and meanings","Column headers"],"may_wrap":["Meaning descriptions can wrap naturally at word boundaries.","Multiword names can wrap; their extra line may fit within the height already required by the meaning."]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r0A: widths [82, 137, 87, 277] · table 584×823px · row heights [39, 151, 171, 145, 171, 145] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 6 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0B: widths [82, 108, 87, 306] · table 584×744px · row heights [39, 125, 171, 145, 145, 118] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 6 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0C: widths [105, 126, 105, 247] · table 584×929px · row heights [39, 151, 197, 171, 197, 171] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 7 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
